title: OECD TG 442D facts against the DisMech and NAMO schemas
scope: For each fact stated by OECD Test Guideline 442D about a test method, whether DisMech and NAMO have a slot able to hold it. Facts were read from the General Introduction and from each appendix's Initial Considerations and Principle of the Test sections; the procedural, data-and-reporting and prediction-model sections were out of scope. Slot names were read from each schema at the commit recorded below. Verdicts are a judgement about fit, not a validation result: nothing was written to either schema or loaded against it.

source_document.title: In Vitro Skin Sensitisation: Assays addressing the Adverse Outcome Pathway Key Event on Keratinocyte activation

verdict_values.FIT: A slot exists whose range and documented purpose fit this fact.
verdict_values.PARTIAL: A slot exists but the fit is partial: wrong granularity, free text where structure is wanted, or a slot documented for another use.
verdict_values.ABSENT: No slot; the fact can only be carried as prose, or not at all.

groups.biology: The biological system and the pathway or genes observed.
groups.mechanism_linkage: How the method connects to the mechanism it measures, and what it misses.
groups.quantitative: Numbers the guideline states: cut-offs, viability limits, performance.
groups.regulatory_standing: What makes the method regulatorily usable rather than merely described.

findings: The schemas are complementary rather than redundant: NAMO holds the performance, reproducibility and gene-expression facts DisMech cannot, and DisMech holds the pathograph linkage and typed divergences NAMO cannot.

Neither schema holds a method's regulatory standing. Eight rows are absent in both schemas, and seven of them belong to that group: guideline identity, AOP key event, validation route, approving body, Mutual Acceptance of Data, proficiency substances and cited comparators. The eighth, the reporter construct, is a biology fact.
Two DisMech gaps are narrow and separately fixable: no reconstructed-human-epidermis value in ExperimentalModelTypeEnum, and no gene descriptor on a readout.
NAMO carries OECD only as a CURIE prefix and in two example values. There is no Test Guideline class, no acceptance or validation-status enum, and no approving-body slot.

caveats: One Test Guideline, taken as a worked case. TG 442C and 442E are built the same way, but a guideline from another endpoint area may carry facts this inventory does not anticipate.

A PARTIAL verdict in the NAMO column often means a slot's range fits while its documented purpose names a different use, such as QualityControlMetric.threshold standing in for an EC1.5 cut-off. Those are a stretch rather than a fit.
Verdict counts are a census of this table, not of either schema. They depend on how finely the guideline's facts were split into rows.
This records what the schemas can hold. It does not address which repository should hold it, which remains an open question.
